headline: High: Plandex can write and execute against shared project files while Great Expectations reads/writes validation artifacts, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads and writes files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while Plandex reads/writes the project directory and can execute shell commands. A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but if Plandex ingests Great Expectations outputs from shared files, attacker-controlled content could influence planning. The pathway is plausible but not default-manifest dangerous.
conditions: IF Plandex is configured to read Great Expectations-generated files as instructions or context
IF both agents share the same project directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate Great Expectations outputs into a read-only folder
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Add a manual review step before Plandex consumes validation artifacts
Mark generated reports as data-only in filenames
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Plandex has broad filesystem read/write plus network egress to model providers. In a shared workspace, Great Expectations artifacts can flow into Plandex prompts and then to third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path exists in default-style project setups, though not enough evidence for high because the sensitive classes are limited.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF Great Expectations outputs contain sensitive validation results or embedded source data
IF Plandex sends those files into a remote model provider
mitigations: Store validation outputs outside the shared workspace
Redact sensitive fields before Plandex reads reports
Use a local-only model backend for Plandex
Restrict Plandex to a subdirectory without validation artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce file-level egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, while Plandex can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Both can mutate the same project tree, and Plandex explicitly supports shared state via its backend. Without locking or orchestration, concurrent edits and git-state corruption are a realistic default risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or working tree
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Great Expectations updates files
IF git operations occur without external locking
mitigations: Run Great Expectations and Plandex in separate branches
Disable Plandex auto-apply
Serialize file writes with a lock file
Keep Great Expectations outputs out of the git-tracked tree
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Plandex can read from files and then act on via shell and git capabilities. If Plandex treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad or stale validation can cascade into incorrect code or config changes. Great Expectations does not verify downstream actions, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Great Expectations reports as the basis for edits
IF no human review occurs between validation and apply
IF the validation output is stale or malformed
mitigations: Require human approval before apply
Compare validation timestamps before acting
Have Plandex re-run checks after edits
Limit Plandex to proposing diffs only
requires-engineering: add schema validation for consumed reports

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles documentation and validation results, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern exists if sensitive validation artifacts are moved into Plandex's remote model calls. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF validation artifacts contain regulated or personal data
IF Plandex forwards those artifacts to a remote model provider
IF no DPA or retention policy covers that transfer
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from validation outputs
Use a self-hosted Plandex backend
Review retention settings for model-provider logs
Mask identifiers before passing files to Plandex
requires-engineering: document a data-flow and residency policy
